episodes.158495: A thunderstorm developed across southeast Minnesota during the afternoon of Tuesday, July 6th. This storm intensified as it moved across the Mississippi River and northeast toward Eau Claire County of west central Wisconsin. This storm bowed out as it moved into southern Eau Claire County where trees were blown down near the Trempealeau and Eau Claire border. Other trees were blown down as it moved across southern Eau Claire County before moving off to the east.
episodes.158517: An isolated thunderstorm produced spotty wind damage and hail over portions of Pendleton County, West Virginia, and extreme northwestern Rockingham County, Virginia.
episodes.158518: An isolated thunderstorm produced spotty wind damage and hail over portions of Pendleton County, West Virginia, and extreme northwestern Rockingham County, Virginia.
episodes.158540: An upper low pressure system spinning over Deep South Texas during the afternoon of July 6th, produced a weak trough axis that extended along the Southeast Texas coast into Southwest and Central Louisiana and Central Mississippi. These upper level features enhanced the seabreeze, with a cluster of showers and thunderstorms quickly spreading inland across Southern and Central Louisiana and Deep East and Southeast Texas. Diurnal heating resulted in temperatures climbing into the lower 90s across Deep East Texas and Central Louisiana on the 6th, resulting in moderate instability within a very moist air mass in place. These showers and thunderstorms intensified as they spread west into the unstable environment in Deep East Texas, with an isolated severe thunderstorm developing over Angelina County, producing damaging winds that downed trees and power lines near Zavalla, Huntington, and Burke. A 62 mph wind gust was also measured at the Angelina County Airport from these storms, before they quickly entered Northern Trinity and Southeast Houston Counties and weakened.
episodes.158554: Scattered thunderstorms developed in a moderate-to-high CAPE, but relatively low shear, environment over eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon of July 6, 2021. Sporadic wind damage was reported from a few storms, along with half dollar-sized hail in Hershey.
episodes.158559: The combination of nearby strong thunderstorms and a passing pneumonia front resulted in several periods of strong wind gusts affecting the Lake Michigan shoreline in the Sheboygan area.
episodes.158607: Hot and humid conditions existed over the mid-Atlantic on July 6, with a cold front well northwest over the Great Lakes and southern Canada. As temperatures rose into the 90s with dew points in the upper 60s and low 70s, strong instability built over the region. A pre-frontal trough and a fast moving upper level disturbance provided some lift, which helped convection develop by mid afternoon. Convection was initially concentrated over northern Pennsylvania and New York, near the better forcing, but propagated southeastward with time. Shear was weak to moderate but sufficient to allow some storm organization into multi-cellular and linear segments. A number of storms became severe, producing damaging winds and some hail. As storms moved southeast, outflow boundaries moving even further south helped ignite additional convection, some severe, which continued into the early overnight hours. The early overnight convection was also noted to be especially prolific with regard to lightning.

episodes.158750: Isolated thunderstorms developed along a boundary located across central and east-central Wisconsin during the late afternoon and early evening hours.  The strongest storms produced severe wind gusts.
episodes.158751: Strong thunderstorms produced gusty winds as they tracked over the Lake Michigan nearshore waters during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.158801: Easterly to southeasterly near surface flow, to the cool side of a zone of stronger differential surface heating and deeper boundary-layer mixing to the east of the higher terrain, resulted in sufficient boundary-layer moisture to contribute to CAPE|on the order of 1000-1500 J/kg. In addition, a belt of 40+kt northwesterly flow around|500mb resulted in strong deep-layer shear. As a result, numerous severe thunderstorms producing large hail developed across portions of the Billings Forecast Area.
episodes.158840: The area of high pressure that had been centered over the Four Corners shifted slightly westward on July 6, 2021. Meanwhile, low level return flow continued which aided in keeping moisture values high across New Mexico. With sufficient instability and shear, another crop of thunderstorms developed first across the high terrain before becoming more widespread across lower elevations. With numerous days of widespread thunderstorms and heavy rainfall, soils across northern and central New Mexico were saturated and primed for more flash flooding. Numerous flash floods were reported across the area with the most significant flash flooding occurring in the Belen area and farther south into Socorro County. Several inches of rainfall breached a canal in Belen which flooded low-water crossings as well as numerous homes and businesses. A State of Emergency was declared in Valencia County due to the flooding.
episodes.159294: A line of severe thunderstorms developed on the northeast side of the Black Hills and tracked across southern Meade County. The storms produced wind gusts around 60 mph.
episodes.159470: A slow-moving low pressure system drew in ample amounts of Gulf moisture on July 6th, allowing for very heavy rainfall to occur across portions of the Lower Rio Grande Valley. Several rounds of rain fell in Hidalgo and Willacy County, particularly in the town of Mercedes where a significant flash flooding event occurred, necessitating water rescues and several road closures.  In total, 6 to 10 inches fell in a swath from near La Joya (Hidalgo County) to the ranches of southeast Kenedy County, including much of the populated Rio Grande Valley north of Brownsville.
episodes.159519: With high pressure in control to both our east and west, the pattern was rather benign across the Commonwealth, with light winds and warm/humid conditions. However, as a upper level shortwave moved overhead, and we reached peak afternoon heating, this was enough to prompt some diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms. A clustered line of showers and storms developed from west to east across the northern half of the state. While this line didn't have much forward motion, there was enough instability, and especially downward CAPE, to lead to some stronger thunderstorms with strong wind gusts. One of these storms brought down several trees near the community Moores Ferry.
episodes.159554: A shortwave trough over the Pacific Northwest began to compromise the ridge in place and introduced a more moist and unstable southwesterly flow to the Northern Rockies. This allowed daily rounds of afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms to develop over Southwest and North-central MT. The period began with discrete supercell thunderstorms developing over the plains, producing severe wind gusts, large hail, and even a weak tornado. The strongest and most widespread activity occurred on July 7th as the Pacific trough and associated wind shear began to exert more of an influence on the region's weather and interacted with the moist and unstable environment already in place.
episodes.159602: Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon and early evening of the 6th across portions of Central New York. Several of these storms became severe with damaging winds. Mainly tree and powerline damage was observed.
episodes.159797: A warm and moist airmass combined with weak onshore winds near a stationary front to produce an environment conducive to the development of waterspouts along the southeast South Carolina coast.
episodes.159865: A cold front moving into a hot and humid air mass triggered severe thunderstorms in the late afternoon across portions of MA and northern CT.
episodes.159866: A cold front moving into a hot and humid air mass triggered severe thunderstorms in the late afternoon across portions of MA and northern CT.
episodes.160022: Scattered thunderstorms moved through southwest Nebraska the afternoon of July 6 and produced damaging winds in Lincoln County and flooding in Custer County.
episodes.160117: Scattered thunderstorms developed across central Nebraska during the late morning hours, then moved east into south central Nebraska during the afternoon. Most of this activity remained weak and of the garden variety, but a few storms became strong across west and northwest portions of the forecast area. Nickel size hail was reported with a storm in Gosper County. Also, training thunderstorms led to a swath of 2-4 inches of rain across portions of Valley County. No impacts were reported. Nearly all of the thunderstorm activity weakened by early evening.
episodes.160206: A storm system over the Great Lakes brought storms into Oneida County during the late evening. One store had damaging winds, knocking down a large tree.
episodes.160276: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours of Tuesday, July 6th, 2021, as an upper level disturbance tracked through the region. Several downed trees and wires resulted from the strongest storms. More than 35,000 customers lost power.||Additionally, heat indices across the Mid-Hudson valley and southern Taconics exceeded 95 degrees during the afternoon hours.
episodes.160362: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours of Tuesday, July 6th, 2021, as an upper level disturbance tracked through the region. Several downed trees and wires resulted from the strongest storms. More than 25,000 customers lost power.||Additionally, heat indices across southern Litchfield county exceeded 95 degrees during the afternoon hours.
episodes.160581: In an environment with temperatures in the upper 80s to low 90s, dew points in the upper 60s to low 70s, and strong low level instability, a subtle surface trough was able to produce scattered storms across north-central Kentucky. This resulted in downed trees and power lines. Lightning started a fire on a power pole and there was one report of severe hail.
episodes.160605: A couple rounds of storms moved across western Wisconsin during the afternoon of July 6th. Wind gusts blew down trees in parts of Buffalo, Trempealeau, La Crosse and Clark Counties. The most extensive damage occurred southwest of Eleva (Trempealeau County) where hundreds of trees were downed in two small forested areas.
episodes.160615: Thunderstorms moved across parts of southeast Minnesota during the late afternoon of July 6th. Winds from these storms blew down trees and branches in Rochester (Olmsted County) and a tree fell on a house in Winona (Winona County) after being uprooted.
episodes.160792: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were a few reports of wind damage with the strongest storms.
episodes.160882: A surface boundary stalled across northern Iowa and southern Minnesota, resulting in multiple days of convective activity. While heat and humidity supplied plenty of instability, kinematic lift along the boundary was weak and deep layers shear was less than 30 knots. While no severe storms developed, the instability created a favorable environment for funnel cloud development. This occurred two days in a a row with funnel clouds reported in Palo Alto county both days.
episodes.160973: A mesoscale convective vortex near Laredo brought thunderstorms into South Central Texas. The airmass was very moist and some storms produced heavy rain the led to flash flooding.  Portions of NW and W Bexar Country received 5-10 inches of rain that morning which flooded Leon Creek.
episodes.160986: Training storms developed over the east slopes of the Sacramento Mountains as modest moisture remained in place with a disturbance moving through north-northeast flow aloft. Antecedent moisture and additional heavy rain over the area northeast of Mescalero lead to flash flooding and road closures.
episodes.161013: A weak shortwave progressed over the Great Lakes on 7/5, providing sufficient upper-level support for a cluster of storms that initiated along an advancing cold front over Lake Michigan to strengthen and go on to produce damaging wind gusts across parts of northern Michigan.
episodes.161141: A pre-frontal trough in an increasingly warm and humid air mass triggered severe thunderstorms across the coastal waters.
episodes.161142: A pre-frontal trough in an increasingly warm and humid air mass triggered severe thunderstorms across Southeastern New York.
episodes.161143: A pre-frontal trough in an increasingly warm and humid air mass triggered severe thunderstorms across Southern Connecticut.
episodes.161144: A pre-frontal trough in an increasingly warm and humid air mass triggered severe thunderstorms across Northeastern New Jersey.
episodes.161145: A line of storms worked across northern Michigan, producing damaging wind gusts along the Lake Huron shoreline.
episodes.161198: A thunderstorm over the coastal waters produced a waterspout.
episodes.161325: Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon of the 6th across portions of Northeast Pennsylvania. A few of these storms became severe with damaging winds. Mainly tree and powerline damage was observed.
episodes.161356: A long duration flash flooding event occurred due a stalled frontal boundary in place helping to supply environmental lift along with ample Gulf moisture to produce slow-moving clusters of showers and thunderstorms. This event was not consistent, but came in waves beginning early July 6th lasting through early July 7th.
episodes.161379: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours of Tuesday, July 6th, 2021, as an upper level disturbance tracked through the region. The strongest storms resulted in some downed trees.

episodes.161558: An isolated thunderstorm caused severe wind damage.
episodes.161572: Another active day with showers and thunderstorms occurring across southern Colorado, especially along the eastern mountains and into the I-25 corridor. While there was an isolated severe threat, the main risk on this day was heavy rainfall with flash flooding.
episodes.161604: Heavy rain led to a few flooding reports across southwest Alabama.
episodes.161675: Thunderstorms produced wind gusts from 35 to 40 knots from near Corpus Christi north to San Antonio Bay during the early morning hours of the 6th.
episodes.161701: A couple rain squalls occurring well outside the core circulation of Tropical Storm Elsa produced brief gale-force wind gusts along the reef offshore Key Largo.
episodes.161734: A somewhat unstable air mass was in place ahead of a warm front that was being forced by a convectively-enhanced shortwave crossing southern Ontario.  This feature generated extensive strong to severe convection from Toronto to the Thousand Islands during the late afternoon and early evening. As the line of convection approached the Thousand Islands, the strongest cell in the line initiated a bow that supported a severe thunderstorm warning.  While there was little shear, downdraft CAPE was approaching 1000 J/kg, which likely tipped the scales.
episodes.161737: A weak mid-level trough crossed the eastern Great Lakes from late morning through mid afternoon, providing weak large scale ascent.  A very warm and moist air mass was in place with surface dewpoints in the lower 70s and temperatures warming into the 80s, contributing to moderate to strong instability.  Shear was very weak, with effective deep layer shear only 15-20 knots. The weakly forced and weakly sheared environment in the presence of strong instability supported a pulse storm mode, with rapidly developing cores which briefly became severe and then quickly collapsed. Initial convective development was mainly along lake breeze boundaries, with subsequent convection developing along eastward propagating outflow boundaries that crossed most of the area.
episodes.161819: A slow moving surface to mid level low pressure system developed over the Coastal Bend of south Texas on July 6th. This was the start of a multi-day heavy rain event across the Coastal Bend as the low pressure system remained nearly stationary through the 8th of July. Locally heavy rainfall caused flooding Rockport and Flour Bluff on the 6th.
episodes.161829: Heavy rainfall over several days led to major flooding on some rivers and creeks in south Texas from July 6th through July 9th. The Aransas River and Oso and Copano Creeks went into major flood stage due to the heavy rainfall.
episodes.161833: A multi-day heavy rain event occurred over the Coastal Bend to the Victoria Crossroads from July 6th through 9th. The total rain amounts ranged from 10 to 15 inches from Nueces County north through the Victoria Crossroads with amounts from 15 to 18 inches over portions of Refugio, Aransas, and Calhoun Counties. The heavy rainfall caused damage to the sorghum and cotton crops across this region. Multi-million dollar losses occurred over the Coastal Bend and Victoria Crossroads.
episodes.161871: A cold front slowly moved across the CWA producing some heavy rains across western counties up to 2 inches with flash flooding. Isolated severe wind gusts were observed.
episodes.161883: A short-duration bow echo evolved from thunderstorms which developed on the warm side of a stationary frontal boundary in the presence of weak shear and strong DCAPE.
episodes.161887: Heat and humidity led to strong instability by afternoon, as a weak frontal boundary settled into southeast South Dakota. Strong instability but weak deep-layer shear resulted in brief, intense and generally outflow-dominant storms.
